epigraph: Stone remembers the shape of the fist that carved it.
vignette: The mason drives the chisel into the soft dirt. He does not carve a door. He carves a wall. The stone rises from the mud. It is grey and cold. It smells of wet iron. The Verdant vine touches the wall. The vine stops. It cannot grow through the denial. The Umbral ember touches the wall. The fire goes out. The wall holds. This is the Bastion. It is not alive. It is not dead. It is simply true. It says no. The ground hardens under the weight. The stack grows higher. Below, the old truths are buried in the dark. The Bastion presses down on them. It does not hate the things below. It just covers them. The mason wipes his brow. He looks at the Rift. The Rift leaks light. The wall stands between the light and the dark. It is a line drawn in stone. The line does not move. The conviction is heavy. The stone accepts the burden. It will not break. It will not bend. It waits for the next stone.
codex_note: The Bastion is the architecture of refusal, turning the fluid contest of reality into a static refusal that forces opposing truths to stack rather than merge.
